source_title: Commercial LPG prices hiked by around ₹10 per cylinder

In the run-up to the festive season, oil-marketing companies increased prices of the commercial variant of the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders by nearly about ₹10 per cylinder across the country on Sunday (November 1, 2026).
Further, prices of the 5 kg free-trade LPG (FTL) refill – primarily catering to migrant workers – increased by nearly ₹2.5 per cylinder.
Prices of the domestic variant remained unchanged. Other than the bottled hydrocarbon gas, Sunday also had the prices of aviation turbine fuel (ATF) for domestic carriers surging by ₹1.37 per litre to ₹138.5 for every litre.
This was the fourth such hike in jet fuel prices since it was last slashed in July.
The latest hike has made the 19-kg cylinder in Delhi ₹10 more expensive and would now be sold at ₹2,820. The 5-kg FTL now costs ₹782 per refill in the national capital.
Mumbai also woke up to a nearly similar hike. Prices of the 19 kg cylinder were hiked ₹10.5 for every cylinder to ₹2,775.
Kolkata had the steepest upward revision. The cylinder became ₹17 more expensive and is now priced at ₹2,971.
While in Chennai, prices increased ₹11.5 per cylinder to ₹2,994.5.
Though Sunday’s standalone hike is marginal, it is the third consecutive hike since July and August, when prices of the 19 kg cylinder were cumulatively slashed by ₹380 per cylinder.
Prices of the commercial variant have cumulatively increased by about ₹85 per cylinder refill across the three tranches since then – including the latest hike.
Prior to the reduction in July and August, prices had cumulatively increased ₹1,345 for each cylinder across four tranches since March 7.
The hike comes amidst a rise in projected under-recoveries for LPG in November and December.
Speaking to analysts in the post-results call, state-owned oil-marketing companies observed under-recoveries to range between ₹309 per cylinder and ₹328 per cylinder in November and rise further to as much as ₹370 per cylinder in December.
Separately, they held the softening of benchmark Saudi CP prices helped minimise the under-recoveries in the Sept-end quarter though it had surged again.
Domestic LPG accounts for about 87% of the bottled hydrocarbon gas sold in the country with the commercial segment accounting for about 9.3%.
Overall, according to latest provisional data from the government, India’s consumption of LPG declined 12.1% on a year-over-year basis to 2.614 MMT in October.
However, consumption of diesel and petrol during the period spurred 11.7% and 3.1% during the reported period.
